Transcribed datasets
Notes on the data
  • Northbeam's samples change between posts (all accounts, accounts present in both periods, one-day clicks, accrual or cash). January and February 2026 appear twice with different values for this reason.
  • Weekly index weeks run Saturday–Friday until mid-April 2026 and Sunday–Sunday after. Not published: 29 Dec – 2 Jan, 31 Jan – 6 Feb, 14 – 21 Jun 2026. No weekly index ran Oct – mid-Dec 2025, so BFCM 2025 comes from the Cyber Week reports.
  • The week of 7–14 Jun 2026 was published twice (18 and 25 Jun); the later version is used.
  • Snapchat CPC shows +12.25% in four consecutive weeks (28 Feb – 27 Mar 2026), likely a carry-over error in Northbeam's graphic.
  • Until w/e 10 May 2026, budget share excludes "All other platforms"; the share desk rebases every week to the eight core platforms so the year is comparable.
  • Meta's average first-time CAC fell 33% YoY in Q3 while the median account's new CAC rose in most spend bands. Benchmark against your own spend band.

Meta's peak-season briefMeta for Business guide · 21 Oct 2026 · read ↗
A brief is three decisions
    If you do one thing this week

    Check your largest campaign is optimising for the outcome the business actually values. If not, change it, then leave it alone and read it against an A/B test or Conversion Lift study rather than last month.

    How many ad sets can your budget feed?

    Meta's formula: weekly budget ÷ (cost per result × 50). Ad sets below ~50 conversions a week ran about 28% more expensive per purchase.

      Earnings desk · Meta · quarterly ad price check

      Meta's price per ad is rising fastest in the US, at +23% a year

      Each quarter Meta reports how many ad impressions it served and how much the average ad cost, both year on year. It is a market-wide read on auction inflation, covering every advertiser on Meta, to set against Northbeam's DTC sample.

      Volume vs price, quarter by quarter

      Lines are YoY % changes Meta reports in each release. When impressions grow fast (new placements such as Threads and Reels, and growth in Asia-Pacific), the average price is held down. When impression growth slows, price takes over: the second half of 2026 is that pattern.

      Price per ad by regionYoY %
      Two independent readsMeta's own numbers vs Northbeam's DTC sample
      Quarterly tableMeta Family of Apps
      Earnings desk · Google · quarterly search check

      Google's search growth is coming from more clicks, not dearer ones

      Each quarter Alphabet reports how many paid clicks Google Search served and what the average click cost, both year on year, plus Google Network impressions and their price. It is the search-side twin of Meta's impressions and price per ad, covering every advertiser on Google.

      Volume vs price, quarter by quarter

      Lines are the YoY % changes Alphabet reports for Google Search & other (paid clicks, cost per click) and Google Network (cost per impression). Alphabet gives Q4 click metrics only for the full year, so Q4 points are gaps. Since 2024 Search has grown on volume: clicks up, price per click rising more slowly.

      Runneth (formerly Motion) · Creative Benchmarks 2026

      Roughly one ad in twenty becomes a winner. Volume is how you find it

      Motion analysed 550,000 Meta ads from 6,000 advertisers ($1.3 billion of spend, September 2025 to early January 2026). A winner is an ad that spends at least ten times its account's median ad. Motion rebranded as Runneth in 2026; the Thumbstop newsletter and reports carry on under the new name.

      Foxwell Digital · Foxwell Founders

      What 600 media buyers and agency owners are saying

      Foxwell runs Foxwell Founders, a paid community of agency owners and brand marketers managing over $1B a month in ad spend. It doesn't publish a running data series: its numbers come from member surveys (a yearly agency benchmark and, this year, a Q4 outlook survey with Northbeam) and from field reports in its blog, which posts two or three times a week. Treat this desk as the practitioner view beside the platform data.

      Direct to Consumer · daily newsletter & surveys

      Shoppers are buying from AI shortlists, and brands are discounting on autopilot

      Direct to Consumer (DTC Newsletter) reaches 155,000+ operators five times a week with news, Pilothouse brand teardowns and podcast notes. A few times a year it runs its own surveys of DTC operators and shoppers, usually with a partner. This desk leads with that research, then the sharpest news calls of 2026 and an index of every brand teardown. Sponsored blocks are left out; figures DTC repeats from elsewhere are credited to the original source.

      Their own research
      The Invisible Shelf · AI shopping556 shoppers · 146 operators · Q3 2026

      Shoppers (purple) say AI is already steering what they buy; brands (amber) feel ready but a quarter can't measure it. Published 26 Oct 2026.

      Most brands are repeating last year's discount, and a third of discount-acquired shoppers only come back for the next one. Published 18 Sep 2026.
